name: 普希金

points.title: 贵族童年
points.description: 1799年6月6日，普希金出生于莫斯科一个古老的贵族家庭。他的父亲谢尔盖·利沃维奇·普希金是退役军官，母亲纳杰日达·奥西波夫娜是汉学家汉尼拔的孙女。普希金从小就展现出非凡的文学天赋，在家庭中接受启蒙教育，广泛阅读法国和俄罗斯文学作品。这段时期奠定了他的文学基础，培养了他对自由的向往和对专制制度的批判意识。
points.descriptionEn: Born on June 6, 1799, in Moscow to an old noble family, Pushkin showed exceptional literary talent from an early age. His father was a retired officer and his mother was the granddaughter of the scholar Abram Petrovich Gannibal. Pushkin received启蒙教育 at home, reading extensively French and Russian literature. This period laid his literary foundation and cultivated his aspirations for freedom and critical attitude toward autocracy.

points.title: 皇村学校岁月
points.description: 1811年，12岁的普希金进入专为贵族子弟设立的皇村学校学习。在这里，他接受了系统的古典教育，同时开始创作诗歌。1812年卫国战争的爆发激发了他的爱国热情，创作了《皇村回忆》等早期作品。在皇村学校期间，普希金结识了未来的十二月党人，形成了自由思想和对专制制度的批判态度。1817年毕业时，他的诗歌已经展现出独特的风格和才华，引起了文学界的关注。
points.descriptionEn: In 1811, at age 12, Pushkin entered the Tsarskoye Selo Lyceum, established for noble children. Here he received systematic classical education while beginning to write poetry. The outbreak of the Patriotic War of 1812 inspired his patriotic sentiments, leading to works like 'Recollections in Tsarskoye Selo.' During his studies, he met future Decembrists and developed free-thinking attitudes toward autocracy. Upon graduation in 1817, his poetry already showed unique style and talent, gaining attention in literary circles.

points.title: 文学生涯起步
points.description: 毕业后，普希金进入外交部任职，同时活跃于圣彼得堡的文学圈。这一时期他创作了大量抒情诗和讽刺诗，如《自由颂》、《致恰达耶夫》等，表达了对自由和进步的向往。他的作品在进步青年中广为流传，但也引起了当局的不满。1820年，因《自由颂》等作品被沙皇政府流放至南方。在南方流放期间，他创作了《高加索的俘虏》、《强盗兄弟》等浪漫主义作品，风格更加成熟。1824年，因与南方总督发生冲突，被转流放至父母位于普斯科夫省的米哈伊洛夫斯科耶村。
points.descriptionEn: After graduation, Pushkin entered the Ministry of Foreign Affairs while actively participating in St. Petersburg's literary circles. During this period, he wrote numerous lyrical and satirical poems such as 'Ode to Liberty' and 'To Chaadayev,' expressing aspirations for freedom and progress. His works became popular among progressive youth but drew disfavor from authorities. In 1820, due to poems like 'Ode to Liberty,' he was exiled to the south by the tsarist government. During southern exile, he wrote romantic works like 'The Prisoner of the Caucasus' and 'The Robbers,' developing a more mature style. In 1824, after conflicts with the southern governor, he was transferred to his parents' estate in Mikhailovskoye village, Pskov province.

points.title: 乡村流放
points.description: 在米哈伊洛夫斯科耶村的两年间，普希金与世隔绝，但创作力极为旺盛。他深入研究俄罗斯历史和民间文学，创作了《叶甫盖尼·奥涅金》的前几章、《茨冈人》等重要作品。1825年十二月党人起义失败后，许多起义者的妻子请求普希金为他们传递书信，这使他更加坚定了对革命者的同情。1826年沙皇尼古拉一世继位后，赦免了普希金，但要求他直接向沙皇汇报创作活动。这一时期是普希金创作的重要转折点，他从浪漫主义逐渐转向现实主义，作品更加深刻地反映了俄罗斯社会现实。
points.descriptionEn: During his two years in Mikhailovskoye village, Pushkin lived in isolation but was remarkably productive. He deeply studied Russian history and folklore, writing the first chapters of 'Eugene Onegin,' 'The Gypsies,' and other important works. After the failed Decembrist Uprising in 1825, many wives of the insurgents asked Pushkin to deliver letters, strengthening his sympathy for the revolutionaries. When Tsar Nicholas I ascended the throne in 1826, he pardoned Pushkin but required him to report directly to the tsar on his creative activities. This period marked a significant turning point in Pushkin's work, as he gradually shifted from romanticism to realism, more deeply reflecting Russian social realities.

points.title: 创作巅峰
points.description: 返回圣彼得堡后，普希金进入创作最辉煌的时期。1829年完成《叶甫盖尼·奥涅金》，这部诗体小说被誉为俄罗斯现实主义文学的奠基之作。1830年完成《别尔金小说集》，1833年创作《普加乔夫史》和《上尉的女儿》。1831年与娜塔莉亚·冈察洛娃结婚，婚后生活奢华但也充满波折。1830年代，普希金与当局的关系日益紧张，他的作品受到严格审查。1837年2月8日，普希金在与法国流亡贵族丹特斯的决斗中受重伤，两天后去世，年仅38岁。他的去世引发了全国性的哀悼，标志着俄罗斯一个伟大文学时代的结束。
points.descriptionEn: After returning to St. Petersburg, Pushkin entered his most brilliant creative period. In 1829, he completed 'Eugene Onegin,' considered the foundation of Russian realistic literature. In 1830, he finished 'The Tales of Belkin,' and in 1833, created 'The History of Pugachev' and 'The Captain's Daughter.' In 1831, he married Natalya Goncharova, whose luxurious but turbulent life became a source of stress. In the 1830s, Pushkin's relationship with authorities grew tense, and his works faced strict censorship. On February 8, 1837, he was mortally wounded in a duel with French émigré Georges D'Anthès, dying two days later at age 38. His death triggered national mourning, marking the end of a great era in Russian literature.

supporter.zh: 普希金被誉为俄罗斯文学之父，他的作品开创了俄罗斯现实主义文学传统，深刻影响了后来的陀思妥耶夫斯基、托尔斯泰等文学巨匠。作为俄罗斯民族文学的奠基人，普希金将民间语言引入文学创作，使文学更贴近人民生活。他的诗歌融合了古典主义、浪漫主义和现实主义元素，形成了独特的艺术风格。普希金不仅是一位伟大的诗人，还是一位思想启蒙者，他的自由思想和人道主义精神激励了一代又一代俄罗斯人追求真理和正义。
supporter.en: Pushkin is hailed as the father of Russian literature, whose works established the Russian realistic tradition and profoundly influenced later literary giants like Dostoevsky and Tolstoy. As the founder of Russian national literature, he incorporated vernacular language into his works, making literature more accessible to the people. His poetry blended classical, romantic, and realistic elements, creating a unique artistic style. Pushkin was not only a great poet but also an enlightenment thinker whose liberal ideas and humanistic spirit inspired successive generations of Russians in their pursuit of truth and justice.

critic.zh: 批评者认为普希金的作品存在明显的局限性，他的贵族背景使他对底层人民的真实生活了解有限，作品中有时流露出对农民的轻视态度。普希金对沙皇制度的态度矛盾，一方面批判专制，另一方面又接受沙皇的恩惠，这种妥协性削弱了他的革命立场。此外，普希金个人生活放纵，与妻子娜塔莉亚的婚姻关系复杂，多次卷入风流韵事和决斗，这些行为被批评为不负责任。他的早逝部分源于个人生活方式的选择，这也成为一些人评价其人生不完整的原因。
critic.en: Critics argue that Pushkin's works have clear limitations. His noble background limited his understanding of the real lives of ordinary people, and his works sometimes showed condescending attitudes toward peasants. Pushkin's attitude toward the tsarist system was contradictory: while criticizing autocracy, he also accepted imperial favors, compromising his revolutionary stance. Additionally, his personal life was dissolute; his marriage to Natalya was complex, and he was frequently involved in romantic affairs and duels, behaviors criticized as irresponsible. His early death was partly due to personal lifestyle choices, leading some to view his life as incomplete.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，普希金被公认为俄罗斯文学史上最伟大的诗人之一，他的作品已成为俄罗斯文化的重要组成部分。普希金的形象超越了单纯的文学范畴，成为俄罗斯民族精神的象征。他的生平故事，尤其是与沙皇的复杂关系、流放经历和悲剧性的死亡，已成为俄罗斯文化记忆中的重要叙事。在当代俄罗斯，普希金被广泛纪念，他的肖像出现在货币上，街道和广场以他命名，他的作品被改编成电影、戏剧和歌剧。普希金的影响不仅限于文学领域，还延伸到政治、哲学和艺术等多个方面，成为俄罗斯文化认同的核心元素。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Pushkin is widely recognized as one of Russia's greatest poets, and his works have become an essential part of Russian culture. Pushkin's image transcends the purely literary realm, symbolizing the Russian national spirit. His life story, particularly his complex relationship with the tsar, exile experiences, and tragic death, has become a significant narrative in Russian cultural memory. In contemporary Russia, Pushkin is extensively commemorated—his portrait appears on currency, streets and squares are named after him, and his works are adapted into films, plays, and operas. Pushkin's influence extends beyond literature into politics, philosophy, and the arts, becoming a core element of Russian cultural identity.

self.zh: 假如生活欺骗了你，不要悲伤，不要心急！忧郁的日子里须要镇静：相信吧，快乐的日子将会来临。
self.en: If by life you were deceived, Don't be dismal, don't be wild! In the day of grief, be mild: Merry days will come, believe.

others.zh: 普希金是俄罗斯一切开端和终结的诗人。他是俄罗斯文学的太阳，没有他，我们今天所知道的一切都将不存在。
others.en: Pushkin is the poet of all beginnings and endings in Russia. He is the sun of Russian literature; without him, everything we know today would not exist.

othersBy: 费奥多尔·陀思妥耶夫斯基
